transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because occupational health at the department says I'm not eating enough. 

I mean, most days I just keep it to black coffee... maybe a plain yogurt or a few bites of chicken at night. It's just that sitting down for a full meal feels like I'm letting my standards slip. But they wanted me to get evaluated, so here I am.
When you say that eating a full meal feels like you're 'letting your standards slip,' what exactly are you worried will happen if you do eat that meal?

I'm worried about putting weight back on. Plain and simple. 

If I sit down and eat a regular meal, I know it's going to show up on the scale. And if that scale is up even half a pound... I get this jolt. It just feels like I've completely lost control of myself. When that happens, I end up spending the rest of the day cutting back even harder to fix it, because I just can't stand the idea of gaining the weight back.

Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating and consume an unusually large amount of food in a short period, or do you ever use methods like self-induced vomiting or excessive exercise to compensate for the calories you've consumed?

No, I don't really do any of that. I don't have times where I just eat a ton of food out of nowhere. Like I said, I mostly just stick to coffee or a little yogurt. And I don't make myself throw up or anything like that. I do stay active, you know, being on the force, but I wouldn't say I'm exercising excessively just to burn off calories. I just manage it by keeping my intake low in the first place.
How do you feel about your current body weight or shape when you look at yourself in the mirror?

Well, it's... it's frustrating. When I look in the mirror, I honestly don't see what everyone else claims they see. People at work say I look too thin, but that's not what I'm looking at. 

I immediately focus right in on my stomach and my waist. That's the measure for me. If I don't look lean enough right there, it just... it ruins the whole day. I basically judge whether I can even respect myself that day based on how my stomach looks in the mirror. If it's not completely flat, I feel like I'm failing.
Could you tell me how much you currently weigh and how tall you are?

I'm 5 foot 10. And, well, the nurse weighed me when I came in... I'm at 110 pounds right now. 

I know it's low. My uniform just kind of hangs off me these days, and I've had to punch new holes in my belt to keep it up. The nurse even told me my weight was dangerously low. But honestly, when she said the number, my first thought was just... I could still stand to look a little sharper.
